name: confidence-escalation-v1
purpose: Test whether Jev's confidence can serve as an escalation gate for a cheap-first-pass / strong-model-second-pass cascade, using failure modes the vendor itself documents in docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13.
notes: Groups map to official jaggedness categories: clear baseline, negation/double negation, indirection, numeric precision, context rot, contradictory instructions.
Every item carries ground truth checkable without a model, so Jev accuracy is measured against facts, not against another model's opinion.
The upgrade decision is made by deterministic code from the probability distribution; Jev never decides its own escalation.

groups.clear: Unambiguous case that the vendor describes as the intended System One use.
groups.negation: Double negatives and negation, named in the official limitations page.
groups.indirection: Property-of-property and multi-hop questions, named in the official limitations page.
groups.numeric: Arithmetic, counting and date comparison, named in the official limitations page.
groups.context_rot: Paired items: identical question and identical answer-bearing fact, one clean and one padded with unrelated material. The docs state unrelated material in state costs accuracy.
groups.contradictory: Conflicting rules, self-contradicting state, and instructions embedded in untrusted content.
